title: Castleman Disease
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Castleman Disease (Unicentric Castleman Disease UCD, Idiopathic Multicentric Castleman Disease iMCD, and HHV-8-associated MCD). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists (excisional biopsy, LANA-1, IL-6, CDCN severity criteria), complete surgical resection for UCD, Siltuximab / Tocilizumab anti-IL-6 therapy for iMCD, and Rituximab-based regimens for HHV-8+ MCD. References StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Castleman Disease Version 2.2026 (April 28, 2026).

a.text: Excisional lymph node biopsy is required for diagnosis. Core needle biopsy and FNA are inadequate to evaluate Castleman nodal architecture (regressed germinal centers, onion-skin mantle zones, sheet-like plasmacytosis) and cannot reliably exclude lymphoma.

b.text: Siltuximab 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks is the Category 1 preferred first-line therapy for iMCD based on the phase II randomized trial (van Rhee et al.) showing durable tumor and symptomatic response versus placebo; give with corticosteroids at initiation and continue indefinitely in responders.

c.text: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks is the backbone of HHV-8-associated MCD therapy and markedly improved overall survival in the HIV-positive MCD cohorts; observe after response and retreat at progression. Occult Kaposi sarcoma may flare after rituximab or corticosteroids, so screen at baseline and continue KS-directed therapy for about 3 months after the last rituximab dose.

d.text: Severe iMCD is defined by CDCN criteria including ECOG performance status >=2, eGFR <60 mL/min, hemoglobin <=8 g/dL, anasarca or effusions, pulmonary involvement, or other organ dysfunction; iMCD-TAFRO (thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, organomegaly) behaves as severe disease and is managed as such.

e.text: Complete surgical excision is curative for unicentric Castleman disease with near-100% long-term survival when fully resected; unresectable UCD may be downsized with anti-IL-6 therapy, rituximab, or embolization to enable resection, or treated with definitive radiotherapy (30-40 Gy).

nodes.name: Clinical Presentation
nodes.title: Castleman Disease: Extent of Presentation
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Distinguish unicentric disease (single lymph node region, usually asymptomatic mass) from multicentric disease (generalized lymphadenopathy with systemic inflammatory symptoms). Extent directs the diagnostic workup checklist.
bullets: Unicentric Castleman Disease (UCD): single enlarged lymph node or single-regional nodal mass, often hyaline-vascular histology; systemic symptoms uncommon.

Multicentric Castleman Disease (MCD): generalized lymphadenopathy plus systemic features (fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue), cytopenias, anasarca or effusions, organomegaly, renal or pulmonary dysfunction.
Document HIV status, immunosuppression, Kaposi sarcoma lesions, and autoimmune or POEMS-associated features at first contact; do not start therapy before excisional tissue diagnosis.

options.label: Unicentric: single node or single-regional mass
Multicentric: generalized nodes with systemic inflammation

nodes.name: UCD Workup
nodes.title: Suspected UCD: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Confirm unicentric extent, secure excisional tissue, and exclude lymphoma before any resection planning.
bullets: Excisional lymph node biopsy of the dominant node (entire node preferred). Core needle biopsy and FNA are inadequate to evaluate Castleman architecture and cannot reliably exclude lymphoma.
Pathology panel: LANA-1 IHC for HHV-8, CD20, CD3, CD138, kappa/lambda light chains with clonality assessment; hyaline-vascular versus plasma-cell variant; explicit lymphoma exclusion.
Virology: quantitative PCR for HHV-8 viral load; HIV-1/2 serology; hepatitis B screening (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs) before any rituximab exposure.
Inflammatory and organ labs: serum IL-6, CRP, ESR, SPEP with serum free light chains, CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin.
Imaging: whole-body contrast-enhanced CT or FDG-PET/CT to confirm single-station disease and plan resectability; chest/abdomen/pelvis coverage.
Surgical consult: assess resectability, vascular encasement, and airway or compressive risk; record baseline performance status and comorbidities.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Severity & Staging

nodes.name: MCD Workup
nodes.title: Suspected MCD: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Confirm multicentric extent, establish HHV-8/HIV status, quantify IL-6-driven inflammation, and grade CDCN severity criteria before systemic therapy.
bullets: Excisional lymph node biopsy of the most accessible FDG-avid node. Core needle biopsy and FNA are inadequate to evaluate Castleman architecture and cannot reliably exclude lymphoma, plasmablastic lymphoma, or Kaposi sarcoma.
Pathology panel: LANA-1 IHC for HHV-8, CD20, CD3, CD138, kappa/lambda light chains with clonality assessment; plasmablastic or plasmacytic features; explicit lymphoma exclusion.
Virology: quantitative PCR for HHV-8 viral load; HIV-1/2 serology with CD4 count and HIV RNA if positive; hepatitis B screening before any rituximab exposure.

Inflammatory and organ labs: serum IL-6, CRP, ESR, SPEP with serum free light chains, CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel (creatinine/eGFR, LFTs, albumin), LDH, beta-2 microglobulin; coagulation profile if TAFRO features (thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, organomegaly).
Imaging: whole-body contrast-enhanced CT or FDG-PET/CT to map all involved stations, spleen/liver size, effusions, and Kaposi sarcoma visceral sites.

Severity baseline for CDCN triage: ECOG performance status, eGFR, hemoglobin, anasarca or effusion volume, pulmonary function/oxygen need, and organ dysfunction inventory; dermatologic and pulmonary KS screen.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Severity & Staging

nodes.name: UCD Resectability
nodes.title: UCD: Surgical Resectability Assessment
nodes.description: Workup confirmed unicentric disease. Determine whether complete surgical excision is feasible, which is the curative standard.
bullets: Resectable: single-station mass removable with clear margins without unacceptable vascular, airway, or neurologic sacrifice.
Unresectable: bulky or anatomically critical disease (mediastinal vascular encasement, deep cervical or retroperitoneal fixation) where upfront complete excision is unsafe.
Reconfirm single-station extent on contrast CT or PET/CT before committing to a curative resection plan.

nodes.name: UCD Resected Treatment
nodes.title: UCD, Resectable: Complete Surgical Excision (Curative)
nodes.description: Curative-intent complete resection followed by surveillance; no adjuvant systemic therapy when fully excised.
bullets: Complete surgical excision with curative intent: remove the involved node(s) en bloc with clear margins; confirm unicentric extent intraoperatively.
No adjuvant systemic therapy or radiotherapy is indicated after complete (R0) resection; systemic IL-6 blockade is not required.
If pathology on the resected specimen shows HHV-8 positivity or multicentric features, re-stage as MCD and redirect to the multicentric pathway.

Surveillance: history, examination, CBC, CRP, and contrast CT or PET/CT at 6 and 12 months, then annually for 3 years; recurrence after complete resection is rare and long-term survival approaches 100%.
Incomplete (R1/R2) resection: re-resect when feasible; otherwise manage residual disease as unresectable UCD (downsizing therapy or definitive RT).

nodes.name: Unresectable UCD Strategy
nodes.title: UCD, Unresectable: Downsizing Versus Definitive RT
nodes.description: Select between downsizing therapy to enable delayed resection and definitive radiotherapy for disease that will remain unresectable.
bullets: Downsizing path suits bulky but potentially resectable disease and younger, fit patients who can tolerate systemic therapy and a second surgical assessment.
Definitive RT suits disease fixed to critical structures where resection will never be safe, or patients unfit for systemic downsizing.
Reassess resectability with contrast CT or PET/CT after any downsizing course before declaring definitive management.

options.label: Downsize first: systemic therapy or embolization, then re-attempt resection

nodes.name: UCD Downsizing Treatment
nodes.title: UCD, Unresectable: Downsize to Enable Resection
nodes.description: Shrink disease with anti-IL-6 therapy, rituximab, or embolization, then re-attempt curative resection.
bullets: Siltuximab (anti-IL-6, 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks) with or without a corticosteroid taper to reduce IL-6-driven bulk and vascularity before surgery.

Alternative downsizing: rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks (particularly for plasma-cell variant or when anti-IL-6 therapy is unavailable), with hepatitis B screening completed before the first dose.
Selective arterial embolization by interventional radiology for hypervascular masses as a bridge to resection or when systemic therapy is unsuitable.
Reassess with contrast CT or PET/CT after 3-4 cycles (or 6-8 weeks post-embolization); proceed to complete surgical excision as soon as resectable.
If disease becomes resectable and is fully excised, follow the resected-UCD surveillance schedule; if it remains unresectable, offer definitive radiotherapy (30-40 Gy).

nodes.name: UCD Radiotherapy Treatment
nodes.title: UCD, Unresectable: Definitive Radiotherapy 30-40 Gy
nodes.description: Definitive involved-site radiotherapy for UCD that cannot be resected now or after downsizing.
bullets: Definitive involved-site radiotherapy 30-40 Gy in conventional fractionation (commonly 36 Gy in 18 fractions) to the unresectable nodal mass with image-guided planning.
Short corticosteroid course for compressive or airway-adjacent symptoms during radiotherapy planning and delivery.
Response assessment with contrast CT or PET/CT at 8-12 weeks post-RT; durable local control exceeds 85% in reported series.
Salvage options for in-field progression: re-consider surgical excision, downsizing systemic therapy (siltuximab or rituximab), or re-irradiation only after multidisciplinary review.
Surveillance: clinical review with CBC and CRP every 3-6 months for 2 years, then annually; cross-sectional imaging at 6 and 12 months post-RT.

nodes.name: MCD Subtype
nodes.title: MCD: HHV-8 / HIV Subtype Classification
nodes.description: Workup established multicentric disease. Classify by HHV-8 LANA-1 and viral load plus HIV status: HHV-8-associated MCD versus HHV-8-negative iMCD. This single fork determines systemic therapy.
bullets: HHV-8-associated MCD: LANA-1 IHC positive and/or detectable HHV-8 viremia, in HIV-positive or HIV-negative (often immunocompromised or elderly) patients; plasmablastic features common.

iMCD (HHV-8 negative): LANA-1 negative with undetectable HHV-8 viral load and negative HIV serology; requires CDCN diagnostic criteria (major: characteristic histopathology plus multicentric lymphadenopathy; minor: laboratory and clinical features) with exclusion of mimics.

Indeterminate or non-diagnostic histology: repeat excisional biopsy rather than starting empiric therapy, and exclude lymphoma, plasmablastic lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma, POEMS syndrome, IgG4-related disease, and active autoimmune disease.

options.label: HHV-8-associated MCD (LANA-1 positive or HHV-8 viremia)
Indeterminate histology or mimics not yet excluded

nodes.name: MCD Re-biopsy
nodes.title: MCD, Indeterminate: Repeat Excisional Biopsy (Do Not Treat Empirically)
nodes.description: No Castleman-directed therapy until excisional histology plus HHV-8/HIV status firmly establish the subtype and exclude mimics.
bullets: Repeat excisional biopsy of a different, preferably FDG-avid node; send for LANA-1 IHC, CD20/CD3/CD138, kappa/lambda clonality, EBER-ISH, and lymphoma gene rearrangement studies.
Re-check quantitative HHV-8 PCR, HIV-1/2 serology, SPEP with free light chains (POEMS screen), IgG4 levels, and autoimmune serologies (ANA, RF, anti-CCP) to exclude mimics.

Provide supportive care only (antipyretics, transfusion, albumin, effusion drainage) while awaiting histology; corticosteroids only as a bridge for compressive or organ-threatening symptoms because they obscure histology.
Multidisciplinary hematopathology review is mandatory before any siltuximab, rituximab, or cytotoxic therapy is started.
Once subtype is established, re-enter the navigator at MCD subtype classification.

nodes.name: iMCD Severity
nodes.title: iMCD: CDCN Severity Triage (Non-Severe vs Severe vs Refractory)
nodes.description: Triage HHV-8-negative iMCD by CDCN severity criteria. Severe disease (including iMCD-TAFRO) needs siltuximab plus high-dose corticosteroids; refractory disease needs second-line agents.
bullets: Non-severe iMCD: ECOG 0-1, eGFR >=60 mL/min, hemoglobin >8 g/dL, no anasarca or significant effusions, no pulmonary failure or major organ dysfunction.

Severe iMCD: any organ dysfunction, ECOG >=2, eGFR <60 mL/min, hemoglobin <=8 g/dL, anasarca or large effusions, pulmonary involvement with hypoxia, or iMCD-TAFRO phenotype (thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, organomegaly).

Refractory or relapsed iMCD: no meaningful response after at least 3-4 cycles of siltuximab-based therapy, or progression after an initial response; confirm adherence, infusion adequacy, and that mimics remain excluded.

options.label: Severe iMCD or iMCD-TAFRO (organ dysfunction present)
Refractory or relapsed after anti-IL-6 therapy

nodes.name: iMCD Non-Severe Treatment
nodes.title: iMCD, Non-Severe: Siltuximab 11 mg/kg q3w (Category 1 Preferred)
nodes.description: First-line anti-IL-6 therapy with or without corticosteroids; continue indefinitely in responders with IL-6/CRP monitoring.
bullets: Siltuximab 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (Category 1 preferred) with or without prednisone approximately 1 mg/kg daily tapered over 4-6 weeks; continue siltuximab indefinitely in responders.
Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks is the accepted anti-IL-6 alternative where siltuximab is unavailable, with the same corticosteroid-taper backbone.

Response assessment every 3 cycles: lymph node size (contrast CT or PET/CT), CRP and ESR normalization, hemoglobin and albumin recovery, eGFR trend, and symptom scores; IL-6 levels may paradoxically rise on therapy and must be read alongside CRP.

Prophylaxis and monitoring: PJP prophylaxis during prolonged steroids, glycemic and blood pressure control, lipid panel on tocilizumab, bowel-perforation vigilance (diverticulitis history), and tuberculosis/hepatitis B screening before therapy.
Non-response after 3-4 cycles or any progression to organ dysfunction: re-triage as severe or refractory iMCD and escalate without delay.

nodes.name: iMCD Severe Treatment
nodes.title: iMCD, Severe / TAFRO: Siltuximab + High-Dose Methylprednisolone (Category 1)
nodes.description: Combined anti-IL-6 plus high-dose IV corticosteroids with ICU-capable organ support; TAFRO managed as severe disease.
bullets: Siltuximab 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (Category 1) plus high-dose IV methylprednisolone (for example 500 mg to 1 g daily for 3 days, then prednisone 1-2 mg/kg with taper) started together without waiting for further deterioration.

Organ support in parallel: ICU or high-dependency care for anasarca with albumin and diuresis, effusion drainage, transfusion for hemoglobin <=8 g/dL, renal replacement planning for eGFR <60 mL/min with rising creatinine, and oxygen or ventilatory support for pulmonary involvement.

iMCD-TAFRO specifics: platelet transfusion thresholds per bleeding risk, thrombosis vigilance despite thrombocytopenia, fever workup excluding sepsis before attributing fever to disease, and early nephrology and pulmonology involvement.

Reassess severity weekly: ECOG, fluid balance and weights, creatinine/eGFR, hemoglobin, CRP/ESR, and repeat cross-sectional imaging at 6-9 weeks; de-escalate steroids as soon as organ dysfunction reverses while continuing siltuximab.
No improvement within 2-3 weeks or further organ failure: switch to refractory-pathway therapy (rituximab, cyclosporine A, or cytotoxic chemotherapy) and consider clinical trial referral.

nodes.name: iMCD Refractory Treatment
nodes.title: iMCD, Refractory: Rituximab / Cyclosporine A / Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Second-line options after anti-IL-6 failure: rituximab, cyclosporine A (especially TAFRO), or CHOP-type cytotoxic chemotherapy; trial preferred.
bullets: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 weeks, particularly for plasma-cell-rich or autoimmune-featured iMCD; complete hepatitis B screening before the first dose and monitor for infusion reactions and hypogammaglobulinemia.

Cyclosporine A (target trough per local protocol, commonly 150-250 ng/mL) with corticosteroids, preferred for iMCD-TAFRO with thrombocytopenia and anasarca; monitor blood pressure, creatinine, magnesium, and drug levels weekly at initiation.

Cytotoxic chemotherapy for rapidly progressive or multiorgan-refractory disease: CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) every 3 weeks, with baseline LVEF, growth-factor support per febrile-neutropenia risk, and antiemetic prophylaxis.
Clinical trial enrollment is preferred at this stage (JAK inhibitors, mTOR inhibitors, anti-CD38 or B-cell-directed strategies) where available.

Re-stage with PET/CT after 2-3 cycles of any second-line regimen; durable responders may return to siltuximab maintenance, and allogeneic transplant discussion is reserved for young, fit, multiply-relapsed patients after expert review.

nodes.name: HHV-8 MCD Course
nodes.title: HHV-8+ MCD: Standard Course vs Severe / KS-Visceral Course
nodes.description: Stratify HHV-8-associated MCD by concurrent HIV control, Kaposi sarcoma burden, and organ failure to choose rituximab alone versus rituximab plus cytotoxic therapy.
bullets: Standard course: controlled or absent HIV, no visceral Kaposi sarcoma, no KSHV inflammatory cytokine syndrome with organ failure; rituximab monotherapy backbone applies.

Severe course: KSHV inflammatory cytokine syndrome with hypotension or organ failure, visceral or pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma, severe cytopenias or hemophagocytosis, or fulminant flare despite ART; add cytotoxic therapy to rituximab.
Both courses require concurrent ART optimization in HIV-positive patients, KS surveillance, hepatitis B screening, and antiviral consideration.

options.label: Standard course: no visceral KS or organ failure
Severe course: KICS with organ failure, visceral KS, or fulminant flare

nodes.name: HHV-8 MCD Rituximab Treatment
nodes.title: HHV-8+ MCD, Standard: Rituximab Weekly x4 + ART + Antiviral
nodes.description: Time-limited rituximab backbone with concurrent ART for HIV-positive patients and antiviral therapy; observe and retreat at progression.
bullets: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 weeks as the treatment backbone; add a short prednisone course only for compressive symptoms, then observe; retreat with rituximab at progression (time-limited therapy).
Concurrent antiretroviral therapy (ART): continue and optimize ART in all HIV-positive patients throughout MCD therapy; coordinate with HIV medicine for immune reconstitution monitoring.
Antiviral therapy: ganciclovir or valganciclovir per local dosing for active HHV-8 viremia or severe flare, with CBC and renal monitoring.

Kaposi sarcoma caution: screen skin, lungs, and GI tract for occult KS at baseline because KS may flare after rituximab or corticosteroids; continue or initiate KS-directed therapy for about 3 months after the last rituximab dose.

Safety: hepatitis B screening and prophylaxis before rituximab, infusion-reaction premedication (acetaminophen plus antihistamine), immunoglobulin monitoring, and response review with HHV-8 viral load, CRP, hemoglobin, and PET/CT at 8-12 weeks.

nodes.name: HHV-8 MCD Combination Treatment
nodes.title: HHV-8+ MCD, Severe: Rituximab + Liposomal Doxorubicin / Etoposide
nodes.description: Rituximab backbone plus cytotoxic therapy for KICS with organ failure, visceral KS, or fulminant flare, with ART and antiviral cover.
bullets: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 weeks plus liposomal doxorubicin (preferred when concurrent Kaposi sarcoma needs treatment) or etoposide for KICS with organ failure or severe cytopenias; baseline LVEF and CBC required.
Concurrent antiretroviral therapy (ART): continue and optimize ART in all HIV-positive patients; manage drug interactions between ART, chemotherapy, and antifungals via HIV pharmacy review.
Antiviral therapy: ganciclovir or valganciclovir during the acute flare with CBC and renal monitoring.
Add high-dose corticosteroids only for immediately life-threatening inflammation or airway compression, then taper rapidly because steroids worsen KS and obscure response assessment.

Supportive and follow-up care: growth-factor support per febrile-neutropenia risk, PJP prophylaxis, KS-directed therapy continued about 3 months past the last rituximab dose, and PET/CT plus HHV-8 viral load reassessment after 2 cycles; de-escalate to rituximab-alone retreat at progression once the severe phase resolves.
